plan: [I compute the posterior expected common value given my signal 29. Since the common value is uniform on {20,...,29} and my noise can be 0–9, the conditional expectation is (20+29)/2 = 24.5. In a second-price auction with interdependent values, bidding this posterior mean avoids the winner's curse and maximizes expected profit.]

[My signal s=29 carries no information about the common value because noise is uniform over a range that makes P(s|C) constant; thus C|s is uniform on {20,...,29}. So expected true value E[C|s]=24.5. In a second-price auction, bidding the expected common value maximizes long-run profit and avoids winner's curse. I will bid 24.5.]

[My observed signal S=15 gives no information about the common value C beyond the prior (C uniform 20–29), so E[C|S]=24.5. In a second-price auction with common value uncertainty, a good practical rule is to bid near the posterior mean but shade downward to reduce winner’s curse risk. I therefore choose a conservative bid slightly below 24.5 to maximize long-run expected profit while avoiding overpayment.]
